literal: At the end Xi, in fear and oppression, lost his will and took leave of his sisters the princesses, speaking of one or two beloved concubines.
idiomatic: At the end, broken by fear, he took leave of princess sisters and named one or two beloved concubines.

literal: A princess wept and cursed him: "Because you took too many of these maidservants and greedily chased wealth you brought today's affair—why still entrust questions to them!
idiomatic: A princess wept and cursed: "You took too many maids and chased wealth—that brought today—why entrust them now?

literal: Xi was ashamed and speechless.
idiomatic: Xi was ashamed and silent.

literal: He was ordered to die at his private residence; his sons were struck from the clan registers.
idiomatic: He was ordered to die at home; his sons were struck from the registers.

literal: Xi's daughters were given a little property and maidservants.
idiomatic: His daughters received a little property and maids.

literal: All remaining family wealth was bestowed on the houses of Gao Zhao and Zhao Xiu; the rest given to inner and outer officials, down to those outside the flow, many a hundred bolts, down to ten—his accumulation was such.
idiomatic: Remaining wealth went to Gao Zhao and Zhao Xiu; the rest to officials high and low in bolts from hundreds to tens—such was his hoard.

literal: His palace women made a song: "Pitiable Prince of Xianyang—how could you err in your deeds?
idiomatic: Palace women sang: "Pitiable Prince of Xianyang—how err so?

literal: Golden bed and jade couch—you cannot sleep; at night you tread frost and dew.
idiomatic: Golden bed, jade couch—yet no sleep; at night you tread frost and dew.

literal: The Luo runs deep and the bank is long—how can a traveler cross!
idiomatic: The Luo runs deep, the bank long—how can a traveler cross?

literal: The song flowed to the lands south of the Yangtze.
idiomatic: The song flowed south of the Yangtze.

literal: Northerners in the south, though rich and noble, hearing it played on string and pipe—all wept without restraint.
idiomatic: Northerners in the south, though rich, hearing strings and pipes—wept without restraint.

literal: Xi had eight sons.
idiomatic: Xi had eight sons.

literal: The eldest son Tong, styled Tanhe, secretly entered the home of Interior Governor of Henei Lu Xiu.
idiomatic: The eldest Tong, styled Tanhe, secretly entered Governor of Henei Lu Xiu's home.

literal: At first he was intimate with Tong; hearing of Xi's defeat he killed him.
idiomatic: At first intimate with Tong; hearing of Xi's defeat he killed him.

literal: Tong's younger brother Yi, styled Zhonghe, later met an amnesty and went to court with a memorial asking to bury his father.
idiomatic: Yi, styled Zhonghe, later gained amnesty and petitioned to bury his father.

literal: It was not granted; he with two younger brothers Chang and Ye fled to Liang.
idiomatic: Denied, he fled to Liang with Chang and Ye.

literal: In Zhengguang an edict allowed sons of the Princes of Xianyang and Jingzhao to reattach to the registers.
idiomatic: In Zhengguang sons of Xianyang and Jingzhao were allowed to reattach to registers.

literal: Later Xi's princely title was restored; burial with princely rites; an edict made Yi's younger brother Tan succeed.
idiomatic: Later Xi's title was restored with princely burial; Yi's brother Tan succeeded.

literal: Yi and Chang were born of Lady Shen Tu;
idiomatic: Yi and Chang were born of Lady Shen Tu;

literal: Ye was born of Consort Li.
idiomatic: Ye was born of Consort Li.

literal: Yi's appearance was tall and strong, his bearing admirable; Emperor Wu of Liang greatly valued him and enfeoffed him Prince of Xianyang.
idiomatic: Tall and strong with admirable bearing, Liang Wudi made him Prince of Xianyang.

literal: Yi yielded to his younger brother of the main line Ye; Liang Wudi did not permit it.
idiomatic: Yi yielded to Ye, the son of the main line; Liang Wudi refused.

literal: Later he was Governor of Qing and Ji and garrisoned Yu Province.
idiomatic: He was later Governor of Qing and Ji, garrisoning Yu Province.

literal: Yi plotted to surrender the province to Wei and was killed by Liang Wudi.
idiomatic: He plotted to surrender the province to Wei and Liang Wudi killed him.

literal: Yi's younger brother Shu, styled Xiuhe, stood alone in the family.
idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Shu, styled Xiuhe, stood apart in the family.

literal: Fine in appearance, skilled in breath regulation, and also with military strategy.
idiomatic: Fine in appearance, skilled in breath regulation, with military talent.

literal: He held Director of the Imperial Clan.
idiomatic: He held Director of the Imperial Clan.

literal: Later he too fled to Liang.
idiomatic: He too fled to Liang.

literal: Liang Wudi especially prized him, enfeoffed him Prince of Wei Commandery, later changed to Prince of Ye.
idiomatic: Liang Wudi prized him, made him Prince of Wei Commandery, later Prince of Ye.

literal: Several times a commander, he watched the borderlands for opportunity.
idiomatic: Several times commander, he watched the borders for opportunity.

literal: When Erzhu Rong killed the hundred officials, Shu was then Governor of Ying Province and asked to attack Rong.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong slaughtered officials, Shu as Governor of Ying asked to attack him.

literal: Liang Wudi supplied men and horses and he harassed the border.
idiomatic: Liang Wudi supplied troops and he harassed the border.

literal: At the start of Xiaowu, Commandant of Justice Fan Zihu was mobile office and with Governor of Xu Du De and Attendant Li Zhao attacked him.
idiomatic: At Xiaowu's accession Fan Zihu as mobile office with Du De and Li Zhao attacked him.

literal: Shu held the city and would not yield; Zihu sent Golden Grandee Zhang Anqi to persuade him.
idiomatic: Shu held the city; Zihu sent Zhang Anqi to persuade him.

literal: Shu asked to yield the city and return south; Zihu agreed and they killed a white horse in covenant.
idiomatic: Shu asked to yield and return south; Zihu agreed and they swore on a white horse.

literal: Shu trusted the oath and made no war preparations.
idiomatic: Trusting the oath, he made no preparations.

literal: Parting from Du De he returned south.
idiomatic: Parting from Du De he returned south.

literal: De did not permit it and sent him to Luoyang, placed in Jingming Temple.
idiomatic: De refused and sent him to Luoyang, to Jingming Temple.

literal: Shu at fifteen fled south and had not yet reached wealth and rank.
idiomatic: At fifteen he fled south before wealth and rank.

literal: Whenever he saw clouds on Mount Song drifting south he never failed to stretch his neck and sigh.
idiomatic: Whenever clouds on Mount Song drifted south he stretched his neck and sighed.

literal: When he first left Liang he saw his beloved Yu'er and gave her a gold finger-ring in parting; Shu always wore it.
idiomatic: Leaving Liang he gave his beloved Yu'er a gold ring; he always wore it.

literal: He sent it back to Liang as a token that he would surely return.
idiomatic: He sent it back to Liang as pledge he would return.

literal: Court learned of it and soon ordered him to die.
idiomatic: Court learned and soon ordered his death.

literal: Before long Du De suddenly took madness and said: "Prince Yuan Shu keeps beating me.
idiomatic: Soon Du De went mad crying: "Yuan Shu keeps beating me."

literal: Until death this fright did not cease.
idiomatic: Until death the fright did not cease.

literal: Attendant Li Zhao soon went on mission to Qin Province; at Tong Pass postal station at night he dreamed Shu said: "I have appealed to Heaven; when you reach Long I will not spare you.
idiomatic: Li Zhao dreamed Shu said: "I have appealed to Heaven; at Long I will not spare you."

literal: Zhao awoke and hated it.
idiomatic: Zhao awoke in dread.

literal: When he reached Long Pass he was killed by Heba Yue.
idiomatic: At Long Pass Heba Yue killed him.

literal: Zihu was soon killed by Daye Ba.
idiomatic: Zihu was soon killed by Daye Ba.

literal: Under Xiaojing his son Zhen from Jiankang asked to follow envoy Cui Changqian to Ye to bury Shu; Liang Wudi permitted it.
idiomatic: Under Xiaojing his son Zhen followed envoy Cui Changqian to Ye to bury Shu; Liang Wudi permitted.

literal: An edict posthumously made Shu Grand Preceptor, Minister of Works, and Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: An edict posthumously made Shu Grand Preceptor, Minister of Works, and Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: After burial Zhen returned to Jiangnan as Crown Prince's Attendant.
idiomatic: After burial Zhen returned to Jiangnan as Crown Prince's Attendant.

literal: When Hou Jing fled south, Liang Wudi made Zhen Prince of Xianyang.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing fled south, Liang Wudi made Zhen Prince of Xianyang.

literal: Sending Jing off, he made Zhen Wei's sovereign.
idiomatic: Sending Jing off, he made Zhen sovereign of Wei.

literal: Before long Jing rebelled.
idiomatic: Before long Jing rebelled.

literal: Ye, styled Shimao, was enfeoffed by Liang as Prince of Sanggan and died in the south.
idiomatic: Ye, styled Shimao, was made Prince of Sanggan by Liang and died in the south.

literal: Tan, also named Mu, styled Yanhe.
idiomatic: Tan, also named Mu, styled Yanhe.

literal: Proud, fierce, and coarse; in a drunken interval at both sides of Luo Bridge he abused passersby and was a plague on the road.
idiomatic: Proud and coarse; drunk at Luo Bridge he abused passersby and plagued the road.

literal: His uncle the Prince of Anfeng Yanming often sharply rebuked him: "Your fierce perversity grows with your body.
idiomatic: His uncle Yanming often rebuked him: "Your fierce perversity grows with your body.

literal: In Song there was the Prince of Donghai Yi, of ordinary will and inferior nature—men of the time called him Prince Ass.
idiomatic: In Song the Prince of Donghai Yi was dull—men called him Prince Ass.

literal: I have watched closely what you do—you too may not escape the ass's name.
idiomatic: Watching you closely, you may not escape the ass's name."

literal: Those who heard at the time called him "Prince Ass."
idiomatic: Hearers called him "Prince Ass."

literal: After Xi was executed, Tan's elder brothers Yi, Shu, and five others in succession fled south, so Tan could inherit.
idiomatic: After Xi's execution Yi, Shu, and five others fled south, so Tan inherited.

literal: He was reassigned Prince of Fucheng.
idiomatic: He was reassigned Prince of Fucheng.

literal: At the start of Yong'an his original enfeoffment as Prince of Xianyang was restored.
idiomatic: In Yong'an his Xianyang enfeoffment was restored.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: He rose to Palace Attendant.

literal: Emperor Zhuang said at ease: "Your talent is not that of Xun or Cai, yet in mid-years you were often promoted—because you grew up in Our house, hence the extraordinary appointment.
idiomatic: Emperor Zhuang said: "Your talent is not Xun or Cai, yet mid-career promotions came because you grew up in Our house."

literal: Earlier after Xi's death the sons were poor; Tan and his brothers were taken in by the Prince of Pengcheng Xie—hence this speech.
idiomatic: After Xi's death the sons were poor; Tan and brothers were raised by the Prince of Pengcheng—hence this.

literal: At the start of Xiaowu his elder brother Shu was captured.
idiomatic: At Xiaowu's accession Shu was captured.

literal: Tan saw Shu was elder and worthy and feared he would replace him, and secretly urged court to remove him by law.
idiomatic: Seeing Shu elder and worthy, Tan feared replacement and secretly urged court to kill him.

literal: Shu knew it and wept, telling Tan: "I came before because of family trouble, unable to die, eating in rivers and lakes, accepting their titles.
idiomatic: Shu wept to Tan: "I came from family trouble, unable to die, eating in exile, accepting titles.

literal: Today's coming is not from righteousness to the end but to seek life—how could I hope for glory?
idiomatic: Today I come not from duty but to live—how hope for glory?

literal: Why do you indulge suspicion and forget the meaning of kin from one belly!
idiomatic: Why indulge suspicion and forget kin from one belly?

literal: Your back and waist are indeed grand, yet in goodness there is nothing to praise.
idiomatic: Your back is broad, yet in goodness nothing to praise."

literal: Tan changed color and left.
idiomatic: Tan darkened and left.

literal: When Shu died he never came to mourn.
idiomatic: When Shu died Tan never mourned.

literal: Later he held Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, Grand Tutor, and was made Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, Imperial Clan Director, and Governor of Si Province.
idiomatic: He later held Works, Commandant, Tutor, Palace Attendant, Grand Preceptor, Recorder, Imperial Clan Director, and Si Governor.

literal: Though salary was thick and rank high, greedy seeking grew worse; he sold judgments and sold offices beyond reckoning.
idiomatic: Though richly salaried, greed grew; he sold judgments and offices beyond reckoning.

literal: Impeached by the censor, he was dismissed and returned to his princely residence.
idiomatic: The censor impeached him; he was dismissed to his residence.

literal: Soon he was raised Special Grand Master and sent out as Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Soon he was Special Grand Master and Governor of Ji.

literal: He again amassed wealth; whenever the people paid tax, besides the regular levy he first exacted five bolts of silk, then accepted payment.
idiomatic: He amassed again; besides regular tax he first exacted five bolts of silk.

literal: He loved hunting and fishing and went out every day without fail.
idiomatic: He loved hunting and fished every day without fail.

literal: Autumn and winter he hunted pheasant and hare; spring and summer he caught fish and crab; hawks and dogs often numbered several hundred.
idiomatic: Autumn and winter pheasant and hare; spring and summer fish and crab; hundreds of hawks and dogs.

literal: He said he could go three days without eating but not one day without hunting.
idiomatic: He said he could go three days without food but not one without hunting.

literal: He entered office as Grand Tutor.
idiomatic: He entered office as Grand Tutor.

literal: At the start of Qi's Tianbao, by precedent his rank was lowered; he was enfeoffed Duke of Xinfeng, made Special Grand Master and Opener of the Office with Equal Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: At Qi Tianbao his rank lowered to Duke of Xinfeng, Special Grand Master, Opener with Equal Honor.

literal: Because his son Shibao with Regular Attendant Peng Guiping, drunk, slandered and falsely spoke of portents, the authorities memorialized death.
idiomatic: His son Shibao with Peng Guiping, drunk, slandered and spoke portents; authorities sought death.

literal: An edict pardoned them both.
idiomatic: An edict pardoned both.

literal: Tan was assigned to North Ying Province and died in assignment.
idiomatic: Tan was assigned North Ying Province and died there.

literal: Prince of Zhao Commandery Gan, styled Sizhi, in the ninth year of Taihe was enfeoffed Prince of Henan and held office of Grand General.
idiomatic: The Prince of Zhao Commandery, Gan, styled Sizhi, in Taihe's ninth year was Prince of Henan and Grand General.

literal: Xiaowen deeply loved his younger brothers; because Gan commanded armies on a separate route he admonished him: "Minister of Works Mu Liang in years and vessel may be teacher; Regular Attendant Lu Yangwu in talent may be consulted—you should take them as teachers.
idiomatic: Xiaowen admonished Gan on a separate command: "Mu Liang may teach you; Lu Yangwu may advise—take them as teachers."

literal: After moving the capital he was reassigned Prince of Zhao Commandery.
idiomatic: After the capital move he became Prince of Zhao Commandery.

literal: He was made Commander and Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: He was made Commander and Governor of Ji.

literal: The emperor personally feasted him in the suburbs and admonished: "The principle of punishments and prisons is what the sages found hard.
idiomatic: The emperor feasted him at the suburbs: "Punishments and prisons are what sages found hard.

literal: Yet since there is a state, can one not urge oneself!
idiomatic: Yet with a state, can one not urge oneself?

literal: An edict made Li Ping Director, Tang Mao Marshal, and Lu Shangzhi Staff Officer to correct and assist.
idiomatic: Li Ping, Tang Mao, and Lu Shangzhi were appointed to correct and assist.

literal: When Ping and others remonstrated, Gan utterly did not accept.
idiomatic: When they remonstrated, Gan utterly refused.

literal: The province memorialized execution of a horse thief—by law excessively heavy—and the Masters of Writing, because Gan had just arrived, indulged and did not impeach.
idiomatic: The province executed a horse thief beyond the law; the Masters of Writing indulged him as newly arrived.

literal: An edict said: "The Masters of Writing bent to Our intent—truly it wounds imperial measure.
idiomatic: An edict said: "The Masters of Writing bent to Our intent—truly wounding imperial measure.

literal: Gan is dark in governing principle and imposed heavy punishment outside the law—both may be reported upward.
idiomatic: Gan is dark in governing and imposed lawless heavy punishment—both should be reported upward."
